MFA No.201056/2021 is filed by the claimants and MFA No.201454/2021 is filed by the Insurance Company NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR challenging the common judgment and award dated 30.03.2021 passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raichur in MVC No.291/2019.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal and cross appeal briefly stated are that on 18.01.2018 at about 4.15 a.m., when the deceased Bheemanna was proceeding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-04/EZ-7255 on NH-44 Bengaluru-Hyderabad road, near Velagamekalapalli cross, at that time, one TATA DCM Container bearing registration No.AP-29/U-1488 (for short 'container') which Mahadevi W/O Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil S/O Kishan Rao Patil And ... on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78490987/
4 was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.

entities.text: Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR 4.
Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.19,31,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the appeals and cross appeals are filed.
6. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
(a) On Negligence: The accident has occurred due to the negligence of rider of the motorcycle bearing registration NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR No.KA-04/EZ-7255.
It is very clear from the IMV report, inquest panchanama that rider of the motorcycle is also negligent in causing the accident.
But the Tribunal has failed to consider all these aspects and has erred in holding that the driver of the container alone is negligent in causing the accident.
(b) On Liability: The cheque issued by the insured was dishonored.
The insurer has issued a notice intimating that the cheque dated 26.11.2020 is dishonoured and policy is cancelled from the date of inception.
Therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
But the Tribunal has erred in holding that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
(c) Quantum of compensation:

Firstly, even though the claimants have claimed deceased was earning Rs.25,000/-
per month, they have not produced any document to establish the same.
Therefore, Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased on the higher side.

Secondly, on appreciation of oral and documentary NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side.

Lastly, in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 AND CONNECTED MATTERS DISPOSED OF ON 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.

entities.text: MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

5 7 . On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following counter contentions:
(a) On Negligence: The accident has occurred due to the negligence of driver of the Container bearing registration No.AP-29/U-1488.
Immediately after the accident, the claimants have lodged a complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The police have registered an FIR against the driver of the offending vehicle.
After thorough investigation, charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Tribunal after NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR considering the evidence of PW1, IMV report, charge sheet and complaint has rightly held that the driver of the TATA DCM Container is negligent in causing the accident.
(b) On Liability: The insurance policy has been issued on 01.06.2017.
The accident has occurred on 18.01.2018.
Thereafter, on 26.11.2020, the insurer has issued a notice for cancellation of the policy.
To that effect, they have neither pleaded in the written statement nor adduced any evidence.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on insurance company.
(c) On Quantum of compensation: At the time of the accident, the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

The Tribunal has assessed notional income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- p.m.,
which is on lower side.

Secondly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

RE: NEGLIGENCE:
9.

The case of the claimants is that on 18.01.2018 the deceased Bheemanna was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-04/EZ-7255 along with one Gopal as a pillion rider on NH-44 Bangalore-Hyderabad road at about 04.15 a.m., when they reached near Velagamekalapalli cross, the TATA DCM Container bearing registration No.AP-29/U-1488 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to impact, Bhemanna fell down and suffered grievous injuries and died on the spot.
To prove the case, claimant No.1 has been examined as PW.1 and they have produced 6 documents.
The PW.1 has reiterated statement made in the claim petition immediately after that accident, the complaint has been lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle.

The police have registered an FIR in Crime No.8/2018 for Mahadevi W/O Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil S/O Kishan Rao Patil And ... on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78490987/
6 - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR the offence punishable under Sections 337 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code against the driver of the TATA DCM Container.
Under the Motor Vehicles Act, in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.

No doubt, before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
- 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR "25. In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

entities.text: MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court, however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie,
materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
10.
As per IMV report-Ex.P.3, it is very clear that accident did not occur due to any mechanical defects.
The inquest panchanama-Ex.P.4
reveals that the driver of the Container was coming at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle.

Therefore, considering the IMV report, inquest panchanama, FIR and - 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR charge sheet, evidence of PW.1, the Tribunal has rightly held that driver of the Container alone is negligent in causing the accident.

QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
11.

In respect of quantum, even though claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.,
but failed to produce supporting documents to substantiate their claim.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.
According to the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for accidents occurred in the year 2018, the notional income of the deceased shall be taken at Rs.11,750/- p.m.

To the aforesaid income, 40% has to be added on Mahadevi W/O Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil S/O Kishan Rao Patil And ... on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78490987/
7 account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157].

entities.text: Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.16,450/- (Rs.11,750/- + 40%).

Since there are 6 dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of - 14 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and remaining amount has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 36 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '15'.
Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.22,20,750/- (Rs.16,450*12*15*3/4) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
12. In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

13. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant No.1, wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium', claimant Nos.2 to 5, children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium' and claimant No.6, is mother of the deceased and is entitled - 15 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

14. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 22,20,750  Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of spousal consortium 40,000  Loss of Parental consortium 1,60,000  Loss of Filial consortium 40,000  Total 24,90,750
RE. LIABILITY 15.
In respect of liability, the insurer has issued a policy to the offending vehicle on 01.06.2017 as per Ex.R.1.
The accident occurred on 18.01.2018.

The insurer has issued a notice intimating the insured Mahadevi W/O Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil S/O Kishan Rao Patil And ... on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78490987/
8 regarding cancellation of the policy on the ground that the cheque issued by the insured has been dishonoured on 26.11.2020.

entities.text: Mahadevi W/O Bheemanna And Ors vs Vithal K Patil S/O Kishan Rao Patil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: - 16 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR
The intimation on 26.11.2020 has been issued by the insurer intimating that the policy is cancelled from the date of inception i.e., from 01.06.2017.
Since intimation for cancellation of the policy has been issued after the accident and there was no pleading in respect of cancellation of policy, no evidence has been adduced.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly held that insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

16. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeals are allowed-in-part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.24,90,750/- as against Rs.19,31,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
d) Following the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE'
- 17 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR (supra), the entire compensation the interest at 9% p.a. is scaled down to 6% p.a.

e) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
f) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in accordance with the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
g) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal.

MFA No.201056/2021 is filed by the claimants and MFA No.201454/2021 is filed by the Insurance Company NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR challenging the common judgment and award dated 30.03.2021 passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raichur in MVC No.291/2019.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.
The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.19,31,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
But the Tribunal has failed to consider all these aspects and has erred in holding that the driver of the container alone is negligent in causing the accident.
(b) On Liability: The cheque issued by the insured was dishonored.
The insurer has issued a notice intimating that the cheque dated 26.11.2020 is dishonoured and policy is cancelled from the date of inception.
Therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
But the Tribunal has erred in holding that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
Therefore, Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased on the higher side.
The accident has occurred on 18.01.2018.
Thereafter, on 26.11.2020, the insurer has issued a notice for cancellation of the policy.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on insurance company.
Secondly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.

(a) On Negligence: The accident has occurred due to the negligence of driver of the Container bearing registration No.AP-29/U-1488.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No doubt, before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly held that insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

ORDER a) The appeals are allowed-in-part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.24,90,750/- as against Rs.19,31,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
d) Following the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE'
- 17 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7455-DB HC-KAR (supra), the entire compensation the interest at 9% p.a. is scaled down to 6% p.a.
e) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
f) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in accordance with the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
g) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal.
